desert_p23_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_001.text: Yue woke before the hearing bell with the same dry mouth she had felt on the back stool. She ate breakfast anyway, choosing hot broth rather than let fear become a reason to travel on nothing. The notes lay in order inside her own wrapper: what she had seen, what she had been told, what later records had added. She could find each source without opening every page. Outside, the town's bakery cart rattled past on its usual route. The patient’s daughter would be at the hearing after her changed shift.

desert_p23_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_002.text: Ordinary people had arranged actual time to be in the room. Yue dressed, took the habitual pack and walked there before the bell required it.

desert_p23_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_003.text: The public room smelled of fresh tea and dust from the benches. Han's daughter had written the shared sequence large on the board, with separate headings for crop damage, the printed route instruction and the historic household account. The freight chair would manage the public order; the route officer, district mediator and records staff would make or refer the decisions within their own authority. No single person owned all three matters because they fit beneath one northern line. Aunt Su arrived by the qualified short transfer, seated comfortably under her clinical plan with her daughter nearby.

desert_p23_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_004.text: The younger guide came in her hired chair. Both had agreed to their own testimony interval, and both could leave when care required. The village crop claimant took the front bench beside Auntie Reed, whose actual paid attendance had brought her to town on the scheduled market wagon. The rival publisher's representative sat across the aisle with his correspondent's letter and repair estimate. Du had the checked source copies, Gao the current and old grade comparisons. Bao held the field care facts she could disclose with the patients' permission, keeping private records under their own custody.

desert_p23_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_005.text: The well keeper had sent a signed maintenance and receiving account through the confirmed carrier; his current work kept him in Onion Hollow. Yue found her stool and put the notes on her lap. The room looked back at her without yet knowing what she would say. The chair began by reading the actual scope of each question. Today's public sequence would establish current observations, source corrections and the facts needed for the separate remedies. Private family balances would be heard in a smaller session afterwards.

desert_p23_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_006.text: Injury compensation would use the mediator's review, not be settled by a mapmaker apologising dramatically in public. The crop claim would use the deputy's levels and damage account, with a stated review route for disputed portions. The chair asked whether anyone misunderstood the arrangement. A carter at the back asked whether tea was available before or after his name was called. She said before was probably safer. The room laughed, and Yue found herself able to breathe. Gao gave the route sequence first. She distinguished the formal wind station, lower exchange and valley relay, their different origins and current conditions.

desert_p23_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_007.text: She described the buried work roof that had been misread as a freight ground, the presently restored cart approach and the still closed footbridge. The old drainage grade copy explained a former bypass but authorised no current setting. The route officer confirmed the responsible inspection and source work, then named the next seasonal assessment under its funded scope. The crowd wanted one neat road; the board offered a set of places each with a date. Yue watched several people write the receiving references down rather than argue with the paper's inconvenient detail.

desert_p23_008.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p23_008.text: My field measurements are attached with positions, instruments and current limits. The old records changed the questions we asked; they did not certify today's structure. On the first visit the lower roof stayed closed to our loaded carts. On the second, the footbridge changed under arriving flow and the former cart margin was withdrawn. We used an independently assessed upper pedestrian approach for rescue and prepared a restricted light cart line for departure. Later repair and inspection released the cart approach within its present registered limits. Each event has its own date.

desert_p23_009.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p23_009.text: If someone uses the latest result to excuse an earlier unsafe instruction, the sequence will tell you where the excuse breaks.

desert_p23_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_010.text: Du described the source errors in the maps. His older edition had compressed later seasonal restrictions and made the lower exchange look too simply available. The rival card had copied that symbol and overstated a correspondent's observation of empty handcarts. The letter and printed card lay on modern support copies where the room could compare them. The representative admitted the omitted load limit but disputed how much of the accident belonged to the card rather than the new drainage. The mediator asked both points to remain in the record.

desert_p23_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_011.text: A mistake did not become the whole cause because it was easy to read, and a changed ground did not make the printed overstatement harmless.

desert_p23_012.speaker: du_she
desert_p23_012.text: I have issued the dated correction and contributed to the proper source work. Those acts do not buy the injured guide's agreement that my part is finished. The old map's omission belongs in the causal review, and the newer card's alteration belongs there too. I can tell you which summary I used and how I shortened it. I cannot tell you what the guide would have chosen if she had received a different sheet; she can speak to that herself. I ask you to retain the actual source copies, including the qualifications that made them less convenient to print.

desert_p23_013.speaker: du_she
desert_p23_013.text: They are the parts we needed most.

desert_p23_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_014.text: The younger guide spoke from her chair. The warning had seemed to allow the light handcart load they carried. She had checked the visible outward ground, which had remained firm; the return followed fresh drainage and softened crust. Her own choices, the printed instruction and the changing site all belonged to the event. She would not call herself blameless to obtain compensation, and would not accept sole blame to make an office comfortable. Bao gave the rescue and care sequence within the woman's permitted account. The mother held the blue shawl in her lap without interrupting.

desert_p23_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_015.text: Yue saw the guide's hand tighten when the rival representative began another question, then loosen as the mediator asked it in a clearer form. The question was whether a larger warning would have changed her route. The guide said a clear prohibition on loaded use would have made her take the ridge, even though the handcart seemed small beside freight wagons. That was her present account of a past choice, not an experiment anybody could repeat. The mediator recorded it with that limit.

desert_p23_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_016.text: The repair maker's actual axle and wheel estimate followed, alongside verified lost-work intervals subject to the woman's medical and employment records. The representative's earlier release offer had not covered even the known cart cost. He looked away when that fact was read. The guide did not smile at his discomfort. Auntie Reed gave the grass village's local observations next. Her grandson had crossed the old causeway dry before the bank changes; later water reached beneath the stones. The sample stems and damaged rows were shown only for the field account they represented.

desert_p23_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_017.text: The deputy's measured junction supported a diverted contribution to the claimant's lower row, with other losses excluded or left for review where evidence differed. The claimant asked for the remedy to include the crop she could no longer plant that season, not just a repaired ditch next year. The district officer explained the damage review and interim provision available now. They agreed the stated amount and retained the disputed remainder for the named follow-up. Then the chair called Yue. She rose by habit, saw the stool and sat again after permission she did not need to make dramatic.

desert_p23_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_018.text: She gave her name and the work she had done on the first two journeys. A carrier broker asked whether her fifth cultivation stage qualified her to judge the channel's source. She said her earned stage had its own guarded receiving tasks and limits; field source and structural assessments belonged to the professionals and controls she had witnessed. The broker looked disappointed. The chair asked him what specific observation he wanted. He asked about the stored water at the northern house, and Yue opened the page that actually answered it.

desert_p23_019.speaker: lin_yue
desert_p23_019.text: The crew drew one hundred and ninety litres from that store on the day recorded. Twenty went to flushing and samples. One hundred and seventy was the raw water put into the two loaned service casks for treatment. The actual cooled clean batch credit was one hundred and fifty-eight, after evaporation and handling loss. We did not add the whole source draw to our travelling tanks. The record separates those quantities, and the source estimate did not become a later refill promise. The casks were returned to their keeper and inspected before our first return to town.

desert_p23_020.speaker: lin_yue
desert_p23_020.text: I was present for those acts.

desert_p23_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_021.text: The broker had written one hundred and ninety credited on his question slip. He crossed out the last word. Bao confirmed the field controls and treatment sequence within its actual source scope. Boiling had followed screening that found the stored rain draw within the applicable limits; it had not been offered as a way to remove salt from uncertain channel water. The water officer retained that distinction in the public note. Yue noticed her hand was shaking less. The question had looked like an accusation until the quantities found their proper places.

desert_p23_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_022.text: They had not become easier because she was brave. They had become clearer because the notebook contained the count made when it mattered.

desert_p23_023.speaker: lin_yue
desert_p23_023.text: On the first return, the damaged outlet lost one hundred and sixty litres before ordinary manual closure stopped it. Eleven were caught directly from the tank stream in a clean vessel, before touching the ground. After treatment, the actual recovered clean credit was ten. The net loss was one hundred and fifty. By the final day our routine stock could not meet the actual necessary withdrawal. Han opened the protected compartment and measured five litres for essential use. The final tank stock was one hundred and ninety-five. Nobody was asked to hide thirst in order to preserve the thread.

desert_p23_024.speaker: lin_yue
desert_p23_024.text: I saw the thread cut and the draw recorded.

desert_p23_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_025.text: Han gave the workshop's later finding on the concealed collar defect and revised service inspection. The driver had been paid and had witnessed the examination; his wages had not supplied a convenient damage fund. The chair asked whether the first essential reserve draw had altered the second trip's protected provision. It had not. The later reserve tanks were separately assigned and filled, with two protected hundreds included in their actual initial thirteen hundred. Yue heard the dates settle on the board one by one. A story told too quickly could make every water loss happen to the same tank forever.

desert_p23_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_026.text: The actual sequence had three different journeys and several different vessels, all of them capable of being named. The broker's next question concerned the three hundred litres transferred to Onion Hollow. Why keep protected stock when a well was closed? Gao asked him to consider the decision from the departure morning rather than the later safe arrival. Five hundred and ten remaining had to carry twelve adults, four mules and two days of essential need, with heat, treatment and delay still uncertain.

desert_p23_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_027.text: The ordinary two-day forecast was two hundred and sixty-four, leaving only forty-six routine litres above that forecast when the two protected hundreds stayed visible. A further fifty transferred would already make the ordinary forecast draw on contingency before any extra need. The calculation did not prove one morally perfect number. It showed what risk the team was actually deciding to carry.

desert_p23_028.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p23_028.text: We had confirmed clean receiving capacity for three hundred, the community's own reserve and separately counted household stores, and urgent supply requests travelling through real routes. We had three patients to take to fuller care and a restricted cart passage we could use after lightening the load. The transfer served the community and the evacuation. I am willing to be asked whether the balance was reasonable. I will not answer by pretending I knew the final day's exact heat and medical draw. The eventual two hundred and thirty-four still in the tanks was an outcome.

desert_p23_029.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p23_029.text: On the morning we acted, it was not a quantity available to reassure us.

desert_p23_030.speaker: lin_yue
desert_p23_030.text: I counted the actual twenty fifteen-litre vessel loads beside the keeper. Ten went into each cistern. Their own remaining stocks were twenty and thirty, and the settled totals were one hundred and seventy and one hundred and eighty. The first caravan tank lost three hundred. Its protected hundred stayed intact. I saw the receiving count, the clean carrying path and the signatures. I can tell you those facts. The keeper's broader household distribution and later municipal deliveries are in his signed account, not in my private memory of a court I had already left.

desert_p23_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_031.text: The records clerk read the keeper's actual delivery receipts and later source clearance sequence. The first municipal two hundred arrived after household draws had made room within the cisterns' combined four hundred capacity. Later smaller loads were fitted to actual free space. The well reopened after cover work, controlled flushing and responsible repeated source checks, not after a map declared it suitable. The broker asked no further capacity question. He remained dissatisfied with the protected reserve, but his dissatisfaction now had a narrower shape.

desert_p23_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_032.text: The chair invited him to submit an alternative risk provision for future funded trips rather than rewrite the actual morning through hindsight. Bao explained the three local patients' care and transport only to the extent they had allowed. She gave the initial limitations, actual high dry approach, qualified examination, supported low stretcher lift, monitoring and independent clinic handover. She did not invite the room to diagnose Aunt Su from a public account. The two younger workers could walk the firm return under assessed limits; the older woman needed carriage.

desert_p23_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_033.text: The first cart's service deck, restraints and axle arrangement had been checked, with the conservative gross load below the restricted line. The mediator asked the carrier broker whether his concern was a specific load component. He shook his head and accepted the checked manifest for the route question.

desert_p23_034.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p23_034.text: Care continued after the carts reached town. The patients' current limits and recovery plans belong with them and their clinicians. The public record needs to know that a qualified team received them, examined independently and took over from the field support. It does not need the private details of every review to decide whether the caravan used an appropriate transfer route. Aunt Su has chosen to speak here for a short interval under her current plan. She is still recovering. If the room wants her to stand up to prove she is better, the room can want something else.

desert_p23_035.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p23_035.text: We have a chair, and she has a voice.

desert_p23_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_036.text: Aunt Su used the voice at once. The grandmother's receipt, service board and transferred household entry described contributions to a source maintained by living households. The later remainder should be reviewed under the district's rules. She was not asking the freight chair to give her private ownership of a well the community still used together. She wanted the record to stop absorbing household work into a district summary without preserving its account. The chair referred the balance question to the smaller family session already scheduled.

desert_p23_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_037.text: The public correction would state the historical contribution sequence and continuing local maintenance, with private amounts omitted. Aunt Su approved and asked whether she could now have the tea that had been getting cold beside her daughter. The room laughed, and the daughter handed the cup over without making the supported leg move. Yue sat back on her stool, tired in a different way from the road. Telling the sequence had required neither larger qi nor a clever guess.

desert_p23_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_038.text: It had required saying when she had been present, stopping when another person's account began, and tolerating questions whose tone she disliked. Han's daughter came to erase one ambiguous heading on the board while the clerk supplied its proper wording. The room's big public story had not collapsed into one villain or one miracle. It had become several jobs and decisions, each now easier to find. During the break, the younger guide's mother offered Yue a piece of bread. Yue accepted before she realised how hungry she was. The guide asked whether she had been frightened.

desert_p23_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_039.text: Yue said yes, and the woman looked relieved enough to confess she had rehearsed her own first sentence six times. Both laughed softly, their chairs beside the same open door. The mother watched them eat and said she wished all hearings ended with bread rather than more forms. The guide replied that bread could not repair an axle. Her mother said it could improve the people asked to pay for one. Neither statement required a verdict.

desert_p23_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_040.text: The mediator's injury settlement discussion resumed separately, using the verified repair estimate, printed-card overstatement, changed ground and lost-work evidence. The rival office offered a revised contribution toward the known repair and a defined portion of the verified work loss. Du's office offered its own contribution related to the older map omission. Neither offer required the guide to praise the card. With the mediator's plain explanation and time to ask questions, she accepted the bounded settlement for the stated costs, retaining any excluded matter exactly as the written agreement specified.

desert_p23_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_041.text: The money was paid into the agreed repair and claimant accounts under receipts. The handcart's replacement axle acquired a funded date instead of remaining a hopeful future. The crop claimant accepted the interim provision and the scheduled final damage review after the district officer confirmed the measured contribution and disputed portions. The collective's route interest remained separate: any lower freight reopening required current drainage and structural work, with the gardens represented. Auntie Reed signed her actual observations and collected the paid witness-time entry.

desert_p23_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_042.text: She had mats to take home and no wish to become a permanent public expert on every northern stream. Yue helped her find the returning wagon's appointed place. The grandmother checked the receiving wrapper, then asked whether town would finally let her cultivate grass without turning it into an appendix. Yue said the grass would probably continue ignoring the office. The smaller family session began after Aunt Su's rest interval and current comfort were checked. The records officer reviewed the historic identifier, receipt, transferred remainder and later unclosed acknowledgement with the daughter and authorised household representative.

desert_p23_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_043.text: The present review could recognise a valid unresolved account, subject to conversion and the living claim rules, without making the old source contribution an unlimited physical-water credit. A dated decision route and review appointment were issued; the family retained copies. Aunt Su asked the officer to read the grandmother's name correctly once. He did. That mattered more in the room than the public audience would have understood, and needed no separate announcement outside it.

desert_p23_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_044.text: By late afternoon the benches were nearly empty. The clerk had the actual decisions, referrals, receipts and remaining dates, rather than a general promise that the northern matter was solved. Han collected the shared public sequence for the receiving yard. Gao arranged the new current map strip with the apprentice. Bao accompanied the patient transfer back to the courtyard under the agreed short-care plan. Yue remained a moment beside the stool where she had first felt her mouth go dry. A circle of tea marked the floor near its leg.

desert_p23_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_045.text: The hearing had left an ordinary stain and several usable records. She picked up her own notes, ready to carry only the part that was hers.

desert_p23_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_046.text: Outside, the rival office's clerk stood beneath the date board with a folded copy of the settlement. He was the young man who had sold the guide the printed card. Yue recognised him from the counter, though she could not have supplied his name. He asked the guide whether she intended to tell every customer that his office's paper had injured her. The guide turned her chair toward him. Her mother stopped fastening the shawl. Yue stayed beside the doorway rather than answering for either woman. The clerk looked younger without the counter between him and everyone else.

desert_p23_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_047.text: His folded paper shook slightly in the hand that held it. The guide said she would tell anyone who asked what had actually happened. That included her own haste, the dry-handcart qualification missing from the sold card, the later ground change and the axle she now had to replace. She would also say the office had paid the stated share of the settled costs. The clerk opened his mouth, closed it and tried again. He had thought the older print was current because it was stacked above the newer strip. The guide asked whether he had told his employer that.

desert_p23_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_048.text: He said no. She said he should start there. Her mother resumed fastening the shawl, leaving the conversation's uncomfortable centre uncovered.

desert_p23_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_049.text: Yue walked with him to the printing room because the guide's returning chair was ready and there was no advantage in making the two women wait. He did not want a witness to his confession. She explained that she was going there anyway to collect her own corrected public sequence. At the door he asked whether she considered him a liar. She said she did not know what he had believed when he sold the paper. She knew what he had heard today. He frowned at the distinction, perhaps because it left him something still to do.

desert_p23_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_050.text: He went inside carrying the folded agreement, and Yue waited at the outer bench. The rival compiler received the clerk in the shop's open front room, away from private customer accounts. Yue heard the beginning of their conversation, then moved to the street when it became a staff matter. Through the window she saw the compiler take down the upper shelf of old cards and check their dates one by one. The boy beside him looked miserable, but neither man was shouting. A returned traveller came to the counter before the checking was finished.

desert_p23_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_051.text: The compiler sold him a current issue and took back the obsolete sheet he had brought. Yue watched the small exchange. It was less visible than the hearing and would probably prevent more harm. At Du's room, the apprentice was trimming a crooked test print with a knife so sharp she had covered the unused blade. Du reached for the sheet; she moved it away and asked him to wait until her hand was clear. He waited. Yue thought of the former teacher's habit of correcting before the student had finished.

desert_p23_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_052.text: The young woman checked the margin against the approved release copy, wrote the actual date on the replaceable strip and sent the sheet to the proof pile. There were two paid helpers now, both hired for the rush rather than promised lifelong places. One asked why the paper had so much empty ground. The apprentice said the unmeasured ground was an answer too.

desert_p23_053.speaker: du_she
desert_p23_053.text: I once disliked blank space because it made a map look unfinished. My teacher could fill a corner from memory and make the mountains resemble a procession. I spent years trying to make mine look as assured. Now we have enough paper to print uncertainty, which is an expensive privilege if the next shop will sell certainty cheaply. She has suggested a little current-date window rather than a magnificent border. Customers are already asking whether the window makes the sheet less durable. It does. It also makes the important part easier to replace.

desert_p23_054.speaker: du_she
desert_p23_054.text: I have agreed to pay for a second proof after the next actual route inspection.

desert_p23_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_055.text: The apprentice did not smile at his admission. She was counting ordered copies, and agreement had to become a paid proof before it changed her week. Yue collected the public sequence that bore her corrections. Her own evidence was clearly marked as observations from the first and second journeys; the final conservation journey named the six people who had actually travelled. She ran a finger beside the names without touching the fresh ink. For the first time, the public page did not make her feel taller.

desert_p23_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_056.text: It made her feel the limits of standing in one place while other people went elsewhere. The apprentice wrapped it in scrap, adding a dry waiting interval before folding.

desert_p23_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_057.text: Gao was at the municipal steps with the drainage officer, looking over the scope of the next assessment. The new contract funded observation and measured proposals, with actual garden access arranged through the occupants. It did not pay for an immediate freight reopening. Yue heard the officer ask whether the old bypass could be cleared before the first autumn rains. Gao said she could not give that date until the current obstructions and outlet were examined. The officer scratched out the provisional month on his cover note rather than disguising it as an aspiration.

desert_p23_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_058.text: He left the deadline for her first measured report. That was a task she could accept and a date she could be held to. A gardener who had attended the hearing came over with a sack of spoiled onions. He did not pour them on the steps. He set the sack down and asked Gao whether the assessment would cost another crop. She crouched to look at one he held out, keeping her fingers off it until he offered it to her. The soft part reached under the dry outer skin.

desert_p23_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_059.text: He said his daughter had wanted to peel and sell the good halves. The market inspector would not accept them. Gao explained the actual narrow inspection visits and how the occupied plots would be marked before any hired work crossed them. The man asked for the marking date, then lifted his sack. He wanted an appointment, not a consolation.

desert_p23_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_060.text: Yue offered to carry it as far as the corner. He declined because she did not know how to hold the bottom and several onions were leaking. They walked together instead. He had once supplied a caravan similar to Han's and still liked to watch loaded carts leave before dawn. Now he said the sight made him count other people's stock against the missing rows in his garden. He knew the comparison was unfair. Knowing did not remove it. At the corner his daughter was waiting with their barrow. Yue greeted her and stopped there.

desert_p23_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_061.text: The gardener's grievance had acquired measured causes and an interim payment, but his daughter still had spoiled onions to move. The market was closing more slowly than the hearing. A fish seller was attempting to trade the last of his catch for the baker's broken loaves, while both pretended their goods retained full morning value. Han's daughter stood near the flower cart with a bundle of plain paper. Her father had paid her two checking afternoons as agreed; she had saved part of the money and bought her own drawing sheets.

desert_p23_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_062.text: She showed Yue a cart axle from three angles, then a bird whose wings were both on the visible side. She said she knew the bird was wrong. Yue said it might be turning. The girl rolled her eyes and asked why adults excused bad drawings but corrected useful ones. Han arrived carrying a pot with three plants in it. He had agreed to take the flower seller's remaining stock home only after measuring the sunny ledge by his mother's room. His daughter examined the crooked plant and declared that he had bought a patient.

desert_p23_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_063.text: He said everyone in the household seemed to prefer those. The girl handed him the pot without laughing; his mother's cough had frightened her more than she admitted. Yue asked how the older woman had managed that day. Han said she had kept her clinic appointment and scolded him for buying a plant without asking which way her window faced. The answer was reassuring precisely because it contained an ordinary complaint. They invited Yue for supper on the following evening, making it an actual invitation rather than a debt from the road. She accepted and wrote the hour.

desert_p23_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_064.text: Han's daughter asked whether she would sit still long enough to be drawn. Yue said yes if the drawing did not make her look like an axle. The girl considered this unfair to axles. Han listened to the exchange while trying to keep the soil from spilling through a crack in the pot. At his yard he found an old saucer, set the plant on it and checked the crack rather than buying a second pot immediately. Yue wondered how much of his business consisted of giving imperfect things the right support.

desert_p23_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_065.text: At the courtyard, Aunt Su was tired enough to keep her eyes closed while her daughter described the hearing to a visiting cousin. Bao had already checked the agreed receiving arrangements and left the next actual clinic review written where the family could find it. The niece sat at the work table with her sorting boxes shut. She had completed the permitted short task before lunch; there would be no second shift because strangers had praised her usefulness. Yue waited until the cousin left. Aunt Su opened one eye and asked whether the officers had finally learned her grandmother's name.

desert_p23_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_066.text: Yue said they had said it correctly. The old woman closed her eye again, satisfied for the moment. The daughter took Yue aside to ask about the unresolved conversion of the historic account. Yue showed her the dated review line on the family's own copy rather than offering to pursue it personally forever. The receiving officer would compare the old units and the later transferred amount before a present monetary decision. The daughter nodded, then asked a different question: had her mother spoken too sharply to the chair?

desert_p23_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_067.text: Yue said the chair had asked her to repeat a word because the cart passing outside had been noisy. After that he had written it. The daughter looked through the door at the resting woman and laughed quietly. She had expected a reprimand; her mother had asked for accuracy.

desert_p23_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_068.text: The first guide had returned to her mother's rooms after the hearing, with the new repair receipt safely wrapped. Yue did not visit again that evening. Their conversation had ended with a completed invitation to a later public map display, conditional on the woman's comfort and care arrangements; it was not permission to keep appearing at the bedside. Instead Yue stopped at the clinic receiving desk to leave the written public summary for Bao as requested. An attendant put it in the nonclinical tray.

desert_p23_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_069.text: Beyond the screen someone was trying to persuade an impatient child to let a splinter be examined. Yue could hear the child's negotiating terms, which involved a sweet and the right to insult the splinter afterwards. Bao came out while the child was still bargaining. She took the public summary and asked Yue to sit for a moment. A long hearing could leave a witness thirsty even when the witness had not been injured. She handed her a cup from the ordinary drinking supply, not a remedy.

desert_p23_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_070.text: Yue admitted that speaking about the five protected litres had felt worse than speaking about the leaking tank. Bao said she remembered how carefully Yue had measured the final draw. The cup was warm from the afternoon room. Yue drank it slowly, relieved that nobody was recording its amount as part of a demonstration.

desert_p23_071.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p23_071.text: The protected compartment was there for essential use when the ordinary supply failed. You did not fail by opening it under the recorded need. We should still ask why the collar failed and whether the earlier checks could have found that fault; the workshop has not established its age. If we make you ashamed of the five litres, the next person may leave a necessary ration sealed for the beauty of the return figure. I want a reserve people can use correctly.

desert_p23_072.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p23_072.text: I also want an office that buys sound collars before a return figure becomes an excuse for careless equipment. Those wants fit in the same room.

desert_p23_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_073.text: Yue set the empty cup down. She had known the calculation, but had not known how much she had wanted permission to stop reliving it. Bao was called behind the screen before either could make a closing speech. The child had accepted the examination on condition that his aunt remain and the offending splinter be shown to him. Yue left the clinic and heard him accuse it of cowardice. The accusation carried down the corridor with perfect conviction. She smiled at the door, then stepped into the cooler street.

desert_p23_074.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_074.text: The sky was becoming pale rather than red; a wind from the higher country had drawn a thin seam of cloud across the west.

desert_p23_075.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_075.text: Tuo was sitting beside the receiving yard's repaired wheel with a short piece of cord. Yue assumed she was marking a distance and was corrected: the guide was making a loop for the shutter catch in her own rented room. The landlord had offered a new catch next week, but the wind would not wait for the appointment. Tuo's ankle tolerated the day's firm-ground walking; rough carrying remained outside her present clearance. She asked Yue whether she had put her own name on a hearing page today. Yue said yes.

desert_p23_076.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_076.text: Tuo held up the loop, tested it with a pull and said that was how a witness became harder to mislay. Then she asked for the knife, handle first. They talked about the red mast while she cut the loose cord. Tuo had not changed what she knew of her brother's last journey. The cloth had made her stop; it had not supplied his final words or the exact place where he died. A relative had now agreed to visit the old winter freight office with her and compare the existing record after the hearing season.

desert_p23_077.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_077.text: She would pay her own travel and choose the date when her ankle and the route allowed it. Yue asked whether she wanted help with the office letter. Tuo said the letter was written. She wanted somebody to hold the cord while she threaded the catch. Yue did that.

desert_p23_078.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_078.text: Her room's shutter stood at an awkward height but opened above firm ground, so Tuo fetched a sound short stool instead of balancing on the bed. Yue steadied it while she fitted the loop within an easy reach that did not require an overhead catch. They lowered her carefully back to the floor. When the shutter stayed open, a smell of supper from the neighbouring room reached them. Tuo said she had spent years thinking a guide ought to manage alone whatever she managed. Her landlord's old stool had apparently not heard that principle.

desert_p23_079.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_079.text: Yue put it back where it belonged. A woman next door called that the principle could fetch its own onions if it disliked assistance.

desert_p23_080.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_080.text: On her way to her room, Yue stopped at the public date board. A new small notice announced a northbound receiving-house call for copying and carrying work in the hill districts; it did not name her or promise a place. The application would be taken at the next staffed stop, with the actual tasks explained there. She wrote the receiving address in her private notebook. Her own road could continue after the desert obligations ended, but there was time to decide how she spent the few days before that departure.

desert_p23_081.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_081.text: Beneath the notice, a boy had pinned a lost-dog description with an unusually precise account of the dog's ears. Nobody had corrected its measurements.

desert_p23_082.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_082.text: Her room was hot near the ceiling and cool at the tiled floor. Yue loosened the habitual pack, counted the ordinary things she had arrived with and set the desert issue list beside them. The survey flags, field wraps and loaned instrument components belonged to their owners; some had already been returned, and the final signed check would take place in the yard tomorrow. Her own wages and notes were hers. She had no desire to steal a measuring rod as a souvenir.

desert_p23_083.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_083.text: She wanted to remember the hand that shook before she spoke and the chair in which the guide had refused an inadequate settlement. Those would travel without adding weight to a mule. She wrote a short account of the hearing for herself, leaving out the private household name and the clinical details she had never been asked to carry. In the margin she wrote what she had not seen on the third journey. The distinction felt less like a hole in her knowledge now. It was where six other people had lived their own days.

desert_p23_084.speaker: narrator
desert_p23_084.text: Outside, the shutter cord Tuo had fitted clicked once against the wood. A cart passed beneath Yue's window, its driver humming badly and with commitment. She blew out the lamp after the last line had dried, and let the town keep making its ordinary, badly tuned sounds in the dark.
